title: The coefficient class is stable under restriction to a pro-étale base change
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, an integer $n\geq1$ and the finite discrete coefficient ring $A=A_{E,n}$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Put $k=\Fbar$. Let $\overline X$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], let $Y$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and fix a morphism $f:\overline X\to Y$. Let $v:V\to Y$ be an object of the small pro-étale site $Y_{\Proet}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], in particular a weakly étale morphism, and form the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product]
$$
W=\overline X\times_Y V,\qquad q:W\longrightarrow\overline X,\qquad r:W\longrightarrow V.
$$
Then $W$ is a scheme, the square with sides $f,v,q,r$ is cartesian, and $q$ is weakly étale, so $W\to\overline X$ is an object of $\overline X_{\Proet}$.

Let $\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of $A$-modules on $\overline X_{\Proet}$ of étale origin in the sense of [def-sf-fullcd-used-class]. Choose any witnessing étale $A$-module sheaf $\mathcal G$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] and isomorphism $\alpha:\nu_{\overline X}^*\mathcal G\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal F$, where $\nu$ is the comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Membership asserts existence of a witness; a choice of witness is used only to exhibit the isomorphism below. With the scheme inverse images of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] and [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], there is an isomorphism of $A$-module sheaves
$$
q_{\Proet}^{-1}\mathcal F\xrightarrow{\sim}
\nu_W^*\bigl(q_{\Et}^{-1}\mathcal G\bigr).
$$
Thus restriction is again of étale origin, with étale witness $q_{\Et}^{-1}\mathcal G$. Here the same étale-origin condition is used on the arbitrary scheme $W$; no finite-type hypothesis on $W$ is asserted. For $\mathcal F=\nu_{\overline X}^*\mathcal G$ and $\alpha=\mathrm{id}$ these isomorphisms are natural in $\mathcal G$.

proof.text: The chosen fibre product exists as a scheme and its projections satisfy the cartesian universal property by [def-pc-fibre-product], applied to $f:\overline X\to Y$ and $v:V\to Y$. Apply the base-change clause of [lem-weil-pbc-weakly-etale-composition-base-change] with its $U=V$, its $V=Y$, its weakly étale morphism $v$, and its $V'=\overline X$, $h=f$. Its projection is exactly $q:\overline X\times_YV\to\overline X$, so $q$ is weakly étale. This gives an object of $\overline X_{\Proet}$ by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], using the compatible size convention of that site. No finiteness property of $W$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 094U, lemma-base-change-weakly-etale (2); fibre-product universal property as in def-pc-fibre-product

proof.text:
Write $\mathcal H=q_{\Et}^{-1}\mathcal G$. The fixed-coefficient module inverse image in [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] has values in étale $A$-module sheaves on $W$, whose category is the one in [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. The comparison adjunction acts on these module sheaves for the finite discrete ring $A$ by [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] to the scheme morphism $u=q$ and evaluate its natural isomorphism at $\mathcal G$. This gives an $A$-linear isomorphism
$$c_{q,\mathcal G}:\nu_W^*\mathcal H\xrightarrow{\sim}q_{\Proet}^{-1}\nu_{\overline X}^*\mathcal G.$$
The orientation required in the conclusion is $c_{q,\mathcal G}^{-1}$. The comparison lemma is for arbitrary scheme morphisms, so its use requires neither quasi-compactness nor finite type of $W$.

source.place: Tag 09A5, section-morphism, commuting square of inverse images before lemma-morphism-comparison; Tag 099R, section-comparison

proof.text:
By [def-sf-fullcd-used-class], membership of $\mathcal F$ in the class means existence of an étale sheaf $\mathcal G$ and an isomorphism $\alpha:\nu_{\overline X}^*\mathcal G\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal F$. The finite-type $k$-scheme and coefficient hypotheses of that definition hold for $\overline X$ and $A$ here. Choose any such pair for this argument; the class does not carry a chosen pair as additional data. Put $Q=q_{\Proet}^{-1}$. Apply this functor to $\alpha$ and $\alpha^{-1}$. Functoriality gives $Q(\alpha^{-1})Q(\alpha)=\mathrm{id}$ and $Q(\alpha)Q(\alpha^{-1})=\mathrm{id}$. Therefore
$$b=c_{q,\mathcal G}^{-1}\circ Q(\alpha^{-1}):Q\mathcal F\longrightarrow\nu_W^*\mathcal H$$
has inverse $Q(\alpha)\circ c_{q,\mathcal G}$: the two composites reduce to identities by these equations and the inverse equations for $c_{q,\mathcal G}$. This is the displayed isomorphism. The pair $(\mathcal H,b^{-1})$ is an étale-origin witness on $W$. Here we use the explicitly stated existential condition on $W$, not the finite-type hypothesis in the definition's ambient setting. To spell out naturality, for a morphism $a:\mathcal G\to\mathcal G'$ the naturality equation of $c_q$ in [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] reads
$$Q(\nu_{\overline X}^*a)\circ c_{q,\mathcal G}=c_{q,\mathcal G'}\circ\nu_W^*(q_{\Et}^{-1}a).$$
Multiplying by the two inverse components gives
$$\nu_W^*(q_{\Et}^{-1}a)\circ c_{q,\mathcal G}^{-1}=c_{q,\mathcal G'}^{-1}\circ Q(\nu_{\overline X}^*a),$$
which is precisely naturality of $b$ when $\alpha=\mathrm{id}$.
